item.title: General anesthesia is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Sasaki J, Koltenyuk V, Mrazik S et al.

INTRODUCTION: Anesthetic management of hip fracture fixation has two primary modalities: general anesthesia (GA) and spinal anesthesia (SA). Choice of anesthesia often depends on institutional protocols and the individual anesthesiologist, due to a lack of consensus guidelines. Most studies have conflicting evidence and focus primarily on elderly age as a risk factor, without accounting for frailty. This study investigates whether frailty influences the relationship between anesthetic modality and postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study queried the ACS-NSQIP from 2015 to 2020 for patients who underwent hip fracture fixation with open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws or intramedullary implant insertion. Patients were separated based on whether they received GA or SA. Frailty was evaluated using the 5-Item Modified Frailty Index (mFI-5). Patients classified as frail or severely frail were included. Multivariable regression adjusting for age, sex, ASA classification, smoking, and the comorbidities significant on univariate regression was performed. The outcomes examined were mortality, unplanned readmission, and overall complications within 30 days postoperatively.

RESULTS: This study included 24,401 patients under GA and 6193 patients under SA. On multivariable regression analysis, GA was independently associated with increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications among frail patients. Severely frail patients under GA had increased odds of unplanned readmission and all complications. When looking at both frail and severely frail patients together, GA remained a significant predictor of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications.

DISCUSSION: After controlling for ASA classification, our study found that frail and severely frail patients undergoing GA for hip fracture fixation had significantly increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications. Our findings suggest that SA may be safer compared to GA in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation. Frail patients that undergo GA may benefit from increased postoperative monitoring to help mitigate complications.

Two ultimately achieved limb salvage with local wound care alone, whereas the remaining three required amputation. None of the referred patients were salvaged with flap reconstruction. One patient died on postoperative day two from unrelated medical causes, and one was lost to follow-up. Consequently, acellular fish-skin grafting may be a useful adjunct in managing complex orthopedic trauma wounds, particularly in high-risk patients or in settings with limited access to reconstructive surgery. Prospective comparative studies are needed to better define indications, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness.

item.description:

DeMessie B, Essibayi MA, Salim HA et al.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) is effective for chronic subdural hematoma (SDH), but failure rates vary and risk prediction tools are lacking. This study developed and validated a machine learning (ML) model to predict MMAE treatment failure for SDH.

METHODS: We conducted an international, multi-institutional retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent MMAE for SDH between 2019 and 2025. The cohort was split into training and test sets, stratified by treatment failure, with all hematomas from each patient assigned to a single cohort to prevent data leakage. Multiple ML algorithms were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, with gradient boosting selected as the final model. The primary outcome was treatment failure, defined as rescue surgical evacuation or persistent/recurrent SDH requiring retreatment. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic. Patients were stratified into low-risk (<5%), medium-risk (5%-15%), and high-risk (>15%) groups using a priori clinically defined thresholds.

RESULTS: Among 692 treated hematomas in the test cohort, 64 (9.2%) experienced treatment failure. The gradient boosting model achieved an area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.803-0.902) before calibration and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.766-0.889) after isotonic calibration, with excellent calibration (Brier score, 0.053). The most important predictors were age-platelet interaction, platelet-hemoglobin ratio, platelet count, SDH thickness, and age. Observed treatment failure was 1.6% (95% CI, 0.4%-5.7%) in the low-risk group (n = 124; 17.9%), 6.0% (95% CI, 4.3%-8.4%) in the medium-risk group (n = 516; 74.6%), and 59.6% (95% CI, 46.1%-71.8%) in the high-risk group (n = 52; 7.5%) (P < .001 for trend), a 37.2-fold difference between high- and low-risk groups.

CONCLUSION: This ML model stratified MMAE patients into risk groups with a 37.2-fold difference in treatment failure. High-risk patients had 59.6% failure, whereas low-risk patients had 1.6% failure. Risk stratification may improve patient selection and monitoring.

BACKGROUND: Injured females experience improved outcomes after component therapy resuscitation. We hypothesize that females <52 transfused with whole blood (WB) have improved survival, lower blood utilization, and lower complication rates compared with males and females ≥52.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis assessed Trauma Quality Improvement Program Participant Use File patients aged 18-90 transfused WB 1/1/2020-12/31/2022. Patients who were pregnant, transferred, anticoagulated, died <1 hour, had a blood dyscrasia, or severe head injury were excluded. Outcomes were compared between: female and male patients <52, female and male patients ≥52, and females <52 and ≥52, separated by injury mechanism. Univariate and multivariate analyses were applied, with the latter controlled for injury factors, race, medical history, time to hemorrhage control procedure, and complications.

RESULTS: 15 051 patients met inclusion. Male sex was associated with greater need for massive transfusion, higher blood product utilization, and acute kidney injury than females, regardless of mechanism (p<0.05, all comparisons). Among those injured by blunt mechanism, females received fewer of all individual blood component transfusions than males at all ages (all p<0.01). Females <52 with blunt mechanisms had equivalent mortality compared with males, whereas females ≥52 had decreased mortality (20.1% vs 24.2%, p=0.01). Compared with females ≥52, younger females had lower mortality (14% vs 20.1%, p<0.01) after blunt injury despite having worse injuries and receiving more component transfusions. These differences were not seen in patients injured by penetrating mechanism. On multivariable analysis, mortality was higher in males and females ≥52 compared with younger females (all p<0.01), regardless of mechanism.

CONCLUSIONS: After WB, being female and younger was generally associated with fewer blood transfusions, complications, and mortalities, but these differences were more pronounced in those with blunt mechanism. Females <52 demonstrated lower mortality compared with older patients. Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms of these findings.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III, Prognostic/Epidemiological.

BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health crisis, and craniofacial injuries are among the most common consequences. However, nationwide estimates of IPV-related craniofacial injuries remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of non-fatal IPV-related injuries using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS)-All Injury Program from 2018 to 2022. Female patients comprised the majority of cases (81.9%), experiencing an average annual rate of 97.6 per 100,000 compared with 20.4 per 100,000 for males. The highest rates were observed among women aged 20-26 (223.1 per 100,000) and 27-34 years (232.7 per 100,000). Black patients had the highest racial/ethnic burden (62.9 per 100,000), nearly four times higher than non-Hispanic white patients. Common diagnoses included internal injuries (28.9%), contusions/abrasions (28.0%), lacerations (17.4%), and concussions (4.2%). OBJECTIVES: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single academic medical center.

INTERVENTION: None.

PATIENTS: Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation.

METHODS AND MAIN RESULTS: We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation.

CONCLUSIONS: A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

BACKGROUND: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) place substantial demands on pre-hospital systems. Extended pre-hospital times are associated with adverse patient outcomes. The factors perceived as contributing to these delays are poorly characterized across different resource settings. This study aimed to identify and compare pre-hospital care providers' perceptions of factors associated with pre-hospital delays during trauma-related mass casualty incidents across high-income and low- and middle-income countries.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between May and August 2024. Pre-hospital care providers with experience of at least one trauma-related mass casualty incident were recruited globally via professional associations, alumni networks, and social media. The survey comprised expert-reviewed Likert-scale items and open-ended questions. Participants were stratified by national income level using World Bank classifications. Quantitative data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Open-text responses were analyzed using thematic analysis following the framework of Braun and Clarke.

RESULTS: Of 225 eligible responses from 54 countries, 158 (70.2%) were from high-income countries and 67 (29.8%) from low- and middle-income countries. Poor communication and geographical challenges were the most frequently cited delay factors, with agreement rates of 84% and 80%, respectively. Agreement that equipment inadequacy contributed to delays was reported by 75% of respondents from low- and middle-income countries compared with 46% of respondents from high-income countries. Thematic analysis identified eight qualitative delay themes: communication and coordination issues, resource limitations, infrastructure and scene access challenges, hospital capacity and preparedness, administrative and policy issues, training and preparedness gaps, security and safety barriers, and responder emotional burden and stress. Administrative and policy barriers were reported exclusively by participants from high-income countries. Responder emotional burden and stress emerged solely from qualitative responses and lacked corresponding quantitative items. Regular training and prior mass casualty experience were widely endorsed as optimizing factors, with agreement rates of 95% and 90%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-perceived delay factors showed similar patterns across settings, particularly communication failures, while differing in emphasis by resource context. Communication improvement, integrated into routine MCI training and operational planning, may represent a modifiable area for reducing perceived pre-hospital delays.

BACKGROUND: Mucormycosis is a rare but life-threatening invasive fungal infection that primarily affects immunocompromised patients. Data on its presentation, management, and prognosis in the intensive care unit setting remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate 90-day mortality and to explore clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and immunological factors associated with outcome in critically ill patients with mucormycosis.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included patients diagnosed with mucormycosis and admitted to the ICUs of the Hospices Civils de Lyon between January 2014 and July 2023. Cutaneous forms (49%) predominated, especially among trauma and burn patients, while pulmonary and rhinocerebral forms were mostly observed in previously immunocompromised individuals. The number of mucormycosis diagnoses increased nearly threefold over the study period, paralleling the implementation of Mucorales-specific polymerase chain reaction. The 90-day mortality was 47%. In the multivariable Cox model, older age, hematological malignancy, and a higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score at diagnosis were independently associated with mortality, while lower liposomal amphotericin B dosing was associated with mortality in univariable analysis. In eight patients without previous immunosuppression and uncontrolled disease, immune monitoring was performed and revealed decreased monocyte HLA-DR expression at 4556 [4194-6936] Ab/c, in favor of injury-induced immunosuppression. Among them, six patients received interferon-gamma as immunotherapy; four responded immunologically and survived.

CONCLUSIONS: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients is associated with high mortality, particularly in those with hematological malignancies. Polymerase chain reaction-based diagnostics may allow earlier detection, and immune monitoring could help identify high-risk patients, particularly in trauma and burn settings.

item.description:

Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with increased trauma burden and poorer outcomes following open fractures. However, its impact on open upper-limb fractures remains unclear. This study examined whether socioeconomic deprivation influenced physiological status at presentation, Injury Severity Score and Gustilo-Anderson grade, time to surgical debridement, and early postoperative outcomes in patients treated within a regional major trauma network. Consecutive patients presenting between 1 April 2014 and 1 April 2023 with open fractures of the humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, or clavicle were identified. Deprivation was determined using the postcode-linked 2019 Index of Multiple Deprivation. Patients without valid English IMD linkage were excluded. Outcomes were time to debridement, length of stay, 30- and 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, and postoperative infection. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, Injury Severity Score category, and Gustilo-Anderson grade. Of 297 identified patients, 291 were included. Gustilo-Anderson grade distribution differed across deprivation quintiles (p = 0.016), whereas Injury Severity Score category did not (p = 0.637). Time to debridement differed across IMD quintiles in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.017), but there was no linear association with continuous IMD decile after adjustment. IMD decile was not independently associated with length of stay, 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, or postoperative infection. There was no statistically significant association with 30-day readmission (odds ratio 1.196, 95% CI 0.979-1.480; p = 0.080), although the estimate was imprecise. Patients from more deprived areas presented with poorer physiological status, and the distribution of Gustilo-Anderson grades differed across deprivation quintiles. However, after adjustment for measured clinical covariates, there was no clear evidence that deprivation was independently associated with delay to surgery or worse early postoperative outcomes. Standardised trauma care may help mitigate socioeconomic differences in early outcomes after upper-limb fractures.

item.title: Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma, Haemorrhage, Prehospital] [strong match]
Czarnecka Z, McCluskey S, Nadolski N et al.

BACKGROUND: Early identification of active hemorrhage (AH) is a critical challenge in trauma care. Narrowed pulse pressure (PP) has been associated with AH at the time of emergency department arrival; however, its role in the prehospital setting remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the utility of prehospital PP as an early predictor of AH in trauma.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multi-centre study (January 2017 - January 2020) including adult trauma patients at all three level 1 trauma centers in Alberta, Canada. AH was defined as either operative or interventional radiology hemorrhage control within 24 h of arrival, or transfusion of ≥ 4 units of packed red blood cells within 4 h. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to characterize associations between prehospital PP and AH.

RESULTS: 2177 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 68 (3%) had active hemorrhage. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had significantly narrower median prehospital PP (40 mmHg, IQR 29-52 vs 53, IQR 42-67; p < 0.001) and lower median systolic blood pressure (SBP; 111 mmHg, IQR 101-136 vs 138, IQR 122-156; p < 0.001). Prehospital PP demonstrated moderate ability to predict hemorrhage (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.67-0.79), comparable to SBP (AUC 0.74, 95% CI 0.67-0.81). Narrowed prehospital PP was independently associated with AH (odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79), reflecting a 51% increase in the risk of hemorrhage for each 10 mmHg the PP narrowed. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had worse outcomes including increased risk of ICU admission (63% vs 18%; p < 0.001), prolonged hospital length of stay (22 days, IQR 8-53 vs 7 days, IQR 4-15; p < 0.001), and increased mortality, although this did not reach statistical significance (18% vs 10%; p = 0.068).

CONCLUSION: Prehospital PP ≤ 45 mmHg identifies patients at risk for active hemorrhage and given its high negative predictive value, is most useful to rule-out patients without active hemorrhage in the prehospital setting. PP is a useful adjunct to support early recognition of hemorrhage in trauma. This is particularly relevant for trauma centres serving large geographic regions, where prolonged transport times delay definitive hemorrhage control. Its incorporation into the prehospital assessment has potential to help facilitate timely mobilization of hemorrhage control resources that actively bleeding patients require.

item.title: Comparative study of autologous bone graft and bone morphogenetic protein-2 for bone regeneration using a novel rabbit Masquelet technique model.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Yamamoto Y, Fukui T, Kumabe Y et al.

The Masquelet technique is widely used for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects; however, autologous bone grafting (ABG) is associated with donor-site morbidity such as pain and bleeding. Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) has attracted attention as a potential alternative strategy for promoting bone regeneration. Studies on direct comparisons between BMP-2 and autologous bone grafting within the context of the Masquelet technique are limited. The purpose of this study was to establish a novel rabbit femoral Masquelet model and compare the bone regenerative capacity of ABG with β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) loaded with BMP-2. A 20-mm segmental defect was created in the femur of 24-week-old New Zealand White rabbits and stabilized with a locking plate. The defect was filled with polymethyl methacrylate cement, which was removed four weeks later to induce membrane formation. The defect was subsequently filled with autologous iliac bone (ABG group) or β-TCP granules containing BMP-2 (BMP-2 group). Bone regeneration was evaluated 12 weeks after the second surgery using radiographic, histological, micro-computed tomography (μCT), and biomechanical analyses. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated satisfactory bone union in both groups, without substantial difference in union rate. Histological analysis showed cortical continuity and new bone formation in both groups. μ-CT revealed that the bone volume/tissue volume ratio of total calcified callus was significantly higher in the ABG group, whereas the tissue mineral density was significantly higher in the BMP-2 group. Biomechanical testing showed no significant differences in ultimate stress, extrinsic stiffness, or failure energy between the two groups. In this rabbit femoral Masquelet model, BMP-2 delivered with β-TCP achieved bone regeneration comparable to that of autologous bone grafting. These findings suggest that BMP-2 may represent a promising option for bone reconstruction using the Masquelet technique.

item.title: Oxidative stress in osteoarthritis: From mitochondrial homeostasis to targeted delivery systems.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Zhang Q, Li Q

Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic joint disease characterized by cartilage degradation, in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction play a pivotal role. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, driven by inflammation, metabolic reprogramming, and systemic risk factors, leads to mitochondrial damage, impaired mitophagy, and disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, forming a vicious cycle that accelerates OA progression. Although traditional antioxidant molecules show therapeutic potential, their rapid clearance from the joint cavity limits clinical efficacy. Recent advances in tissue engineering and smart delivery systems-such as ROS-responsive hydrogels, microspheres/nanocarriers, and exosome-based platforms-enable targeted, sustained, and on-demand drug release, offering new opportunities to restore redox balance and break the pathological amplification loop. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms linking oxidative stress to mitochondrial homeostasis in OA and highlights the design principles and application status of emerging delivery strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation for next-generation precision therapies.

OBJECTIVE: Although the application of autografts continues to be regarded as the gold standard for the treatment of peripheral nerve injuries, there exists a necessity for alternative grafting materials. This study investigates the effects of a nerve conduit obtained from bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes modified with gold nanoparticles (AuNP) and functionalized with the GDNF neurotrophic factor on repair in peripheral nerve injury.

METHODS: Bacterial cellulose membranes obtained from Gluconacetobacter xylinus cell culture were modified with sericin-gold nanoparticles produced by green synthesis and functionalized with glial-derived neurotrophic factor to become conduits. Gait analysis and electromyography (EMG) measurements were performed at the end of the 8th week. Tissues from the sciatic nerve were obtained for histological and immunohistochemical analysis.

RESULTS: By the result of the 8th week, the BC-AuNPs/GDNF group attained results comparable to those of the autograft group, as indicated by the sciatic function index derived from gait analysis and EMG measurements. Examinations of axon diameters, myelin sheath thickness, and vessel count demonstrated that the autograft and BC-AuNPs/GDNF groups exhibited significantly elevated values in comparison to the BC-AuNPs group.

CONCLUSION: In the management of peripheral nerve injury, the application of BC-AuNP/GDNF yielded healing outcomes that were comparable to those achieved through autograft, both functionally and histologically.

item.title: How have management and outcomes of periprosthetic proximal femoral fractures changed? A comparison of two 8 year time periods in a high volume centre.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Toner E, Madden-McKee C, Goodland C et al.

BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are now the leading cause of major reoperation following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Patients are often frail and surgeries increasingly complex. We reviewed PFFs over two consecutive 8-year periods to analyse trends in incidence, management and outcomes to assess the evolving clinical and service impacts.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted using data from the Fracture Outcomes Research Database (FORD) and the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD) across two 8-year periods (2007-2015 and 2016-2024). Radiographic and clinical records were reviewed. Fracture classification, management, comorbidities and mortality were recorded and compared. A regression analysis was performed to determine co-morbidities that significantly increased the risk of 12-month mortality. In the 2016-2024 period, data on re-operations rates were recorded.

RESULTS: PFF increased from 189 to 320 across the two periods, totalling 509 patients. The incidence of Vancouver B2 fractures increased more than 1.5x, rising from 42/189 (22.2%) to 117/320 (36.6%) patients. Fixation remained the most common treatment across the two periods (75.1% and 63.4%), while revision arthroplasty was performed in 22.8% and 18.4% respectively. B2 fracture management changed significantly with fixation increasing (59% v 9.5%; p < 0.001) and revision arthroplasty rates decreasing (38.5% vs 85.7%; p < 0.001). Time to theatre improved (5-3.7 days; p = 0.028) and a higher proportion of patients returned to their pre-injury residence (30.2%; 57/189 vs 39%; 96/320, p = 0.068). No difference in mortality was observed at 30 days (2.6-3.1%; p = 0.796) or 90 days (5.8% vs 9.1%; p = 0.233) but mortality was higher at 12 months (12.2-20%; p = 0.028). ASA 4 patients increased (14%; 25/179; vs 29.1%; 82/282, OR = 2.526 (95% CI 1.54-4.14), p < 0.001). Re-operation rates were lower in the fixation group than in the revision group (12; 5.9% vs 8; 13.6%; p = 0.095).

CONCLUSION: The incidence and mortality associated with PFFs are rising within our unit, despite improved time to theatre and improved discharge outcomes. This trend may reflect a frailer cohort with higher ASA grades. We demonstrate a shift in practice, with more B2 fractures treated with fixation, achieving good outcomes suggesting fixation may be a safe treatment option in selected frail patients.

item.title: Profound motorcycle risks: a national mileage exposure-adjusted analysis.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [Facial/Neck, General Trauma, Systems/QI] [weak match]
Pottayil F, Rider DE, Parry JA et al.

BACKGROUND: Motorcycle crashes (MCC) account for a minority of vehicle miles in the United States, but their exposure-adjusted burden among trauma admissions is not well defined. The purpose of this study was to compare the injury burden of MCC versus motor vehicle crashes (MVC) using outcomes standardized by annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs (ACS-TQP) admissions from 2017 to 2023 was performed for adults aged 18-80 years admitted after MCC or MVC. Primary outcomes were admission, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality per 100 million VMT using Federal Highway Administration denominators. Motorcycle VMT was used for MCC, and light-duty vehicle VMT was used for MVC. Secondary outcomes included Injury Severity Score thresholds (≥16 and ≥25), severe head/neck injury, open long-bone fracture, ventilation, and return to the operating room. Relative risks (RRs) were estimated using binomial regression models with a log link.

RESULTS: Among 1,419,094 admissions, 334,310 followed MCC and 1,084,784 followed MVC. MCC accounted for 23.6% of admissions but only 0.71% of included VMT. Per 100 million VMT, MCC had higher rates of admission (236.4 vs. 5.49; rate ratio, 43.0), ICU admission (70.8 vs. 1.57; rate ratio, 45.1), amputation (5.06 vs. 0.028; rate ratio, 183.0), and in-hospital mortality (6.4 vs. 0.12; rate ratio, 51.6). Among admitted patients, MCC was associated with higher risks of open long-bone fracture (14.7% vs. 6.6%; RR, 2.22), amputation (2.1% vs. 0.5%; RR, 4.25), and in-hospital mortality (2.7% vs. 2.2%; RR, 1.20).

CONCLUSIONS: MCCs contribute a disproportionately high burden of severe trauma in the United States, with higher mileage-adjusted rates of ICU admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality than MVCs.

PURPOSE: To evaluate a large cohort of eye patients from India for the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes of ocular injuries sustained while playing badminton.

OTS categories 3-5 showed better visual outcomes than predicted by the original OTS model.

Initial visual acuity, lens status, optic disc involvement, secondary glaucoma, eye surgery performed, OTS score and posterior segment injury were statistically significant in predicting final visual outcomes. OBJECTIVE: The authors sought to identify plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1) cutoffs corresponding to a range of high positive predictive values (PPVs) for detecting intracranial pathology on CT and detecting pathology on MRI (when CT is negative) in patients who present to a level I trauma center for TBI evaluation with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores of 13-15.

METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data from the Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury (TRACK-TBI) study, which is a longitudinal, observational study of patients with TBI who presented to one of 18 US level I trauma centers within 24 hours of injury. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours. Plasma samples were analyzed for GFAP (pg/mL) and UCH-L1 (pg/mL). The CT or MRI scan was considered positive (CT+, MRI+) if there was evidence of acute intracranial pathology related to TBI. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (AUC) was performed to evaluate the ability of day-1 GFAP and UCH-L1 to discriminate CT+ versus CT-, and CT-/MRI+ versus CT-/MRI-. A K-fold cross-validation procedure was used to identify GFAP cutoffs for predicting CT+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and for predicting MRI+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and CT- subjects, based on the adjusted PPV thresholds.

RESULTS: Among the 1718 TBI participants with GCS scores 13-15, 633 (37%) had CT+ findings. Of the 1085 CT- participants, 608 underwent MRI at 2 weeks postinjury, of whom 154 (25%) had MRI+ findings. Day-1 GFAP had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 (95% CI 0.80-0.84), and UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.57-0.63) for discriminating CT+ from CT-. Day-1 GFAP had an AUC of 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) while UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.55-0.65) for discriminating CT-/MRI+ from CT-/MRI-. For CT+ prediction, assuming a prevalence of 0.36 (from our data) and 0.1 (from the literature), the median GFAP cutoffs to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 were 2879 (95% CI 2195-4704) and 5191 (95% CI 3779-5426), respectively. For MRI+ prediction among GCS 13-15 CT- patients, the median GFAP cutoffs were 1382 (95% CI 1145-2424) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 and 2317 pg/mL (95% CI 1262-2551 pg/mL) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.98.

CONCLUSIONS: These threshold values can be used as an aid-in-diagnosis tool and assist in appropriate triaging of patients who have sustained TBI to urgent neuroimaging, potential escalation in care, and interventions as clinically indicated.

item.title: β-Blockade reprograms trauma-induced changes in bone marrow exosomal microRNAs.
item.description:
J Trauma Acute Care Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma] [strong match]
Yoham AL, Bible LE, Kannan KB et al.

BACKGROUND: Severe trauma produces sustained sympathetic activation that contributes to bone marrow dysfunction, impaired hematopoiesis, and persistent injury-associated anemia. Although β-adrenergic blockade improves bone marrow recovery after injury, the downstream mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol reprograms trauma-induced bone marrow extracellular vesicle (EV) microRNA (miRNA) expression toward restoration of hematopoietic homeostasis.

METHODS: Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized to naïve, polytrauma (PT), PT plus propranolol (PT+BB), PT with chronic restraint stress (PTRS), or PTRS plus propranolol (PTRS+BB) groups (n=6-8 per group). Propranolol (10 mg/kg intraperitoneally) was administered daily. On day 7, complete blood counts were obtained, and bone marrow-derived EV miRNAs were profiled using the NanoString nCounter platform. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using an absolute log2 fold change ≥1.5 and p<0.05. Predicted pathways were assessed using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, and miR-125b-5p was validated by quantitative PCR.

RESULTS: PT altered 45 EV miRNAs compared with naïve animals, including suppression of miRNAs involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and erythropoiesis. Chronic restraint stress amplified this response, with 93 differentially expressed miRNAs following PTRS. Propranolol altered 12 miRNAs after PT and 43 after PTRS, increasing hematopoietic regulatory miRNAs, including miR-125b-5p, while suppressing several stress- and inflammation-associated miRNAs. Pathway analysis identified alterations in NOTCH, RUNX1, PTEN, thyroid receptor/retinoid X receptor, and histone modification signaling. Quantitative PCR confirmed a 2.4-fold increase in EV miR-125b-5p following propranolol in PTRS animals (p=0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: Trauma and persistent adrenergic stress broadly remodel bone marrow EV miRNA signaling. β-Adrenergic blockade selectively reprograms these networks toward pathways associated with hematopoietic recovery, identifying EV miRNAs as potential mediators of posttraumatic bone marrow dysfunction.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Not applicable-Animal research.

Thirty patients (30/47, 64%) sustained their injury due to a fall from standing height and eight patients were involved in a motor traffic accident. Eleven patients (11/47, 23%) sustained a femoral neck fracture, 24 patients (51%) sustained an intertrochanteric fracture and five patients (11%) sustained a subtrochanteric fracture. Five patients had additional injuries.

This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission.

RESULTS: Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

item.title: The impact of presentations in scientific conferences: Publication and citation rates in trauma surgery.
item.description:
J Trauma Acute Care Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma] [strong match]
Touponse G, Bidwell S, Shank A et al.

BACKGROUND: Understanding the publication rates and citation patterns of conference abstracts is critical for program committees and investigators alike. However, the downstream scholarly outcome of conference abstracts remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that across contemporary US trauma-related scientific meetings, a substantial proportion of conference abstracts would not progress to peer-reviewed publications, and that publication rates and citation patterns would vary by presentation format and conference.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of abstracts presented at four major US trauma surgery conferences from 2017 to 2019. We identified peer-reviewed manuscripts associated with conference abstracts via Google Scholar and PubMed. We collected presentation format, publishing journal, 2024 journal impact factor, and citation count. A cohort of directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts was also analyzed. Mixed-effects Poisson regression models assessed the association between presentation and citation counts, adjusting for publication timing.

RESULTS: Of 1,157 abstracts, 762 (66%) were published as peer-reviewed manuscripts. Most manuscripts were published in the Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery (JTACS) (55%), with 5 in journals with a higher-impact factor than JTACS. On regression analysis, abstracts presented as oral presentations, and published in journals with an impact factor higher than JTACS, were associated with a greater number of citations. When comparing manuscripts presented as abstracts to directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstract presentation was associated with 22% more citations (incidence rate ratio: 1.22; 95% CI [1.16-1.29]; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This cross-sectional study of four trauma societies found that approximately a third of presented abstracts did not progress to peer-reviewed publication, with publication rates varying by conference and presentation format. Exploratory analyses found that among those published in JTACS, published manuscripts originating from presented abstracts demonstrated a modestly higher citation count compared with directly submitted manuscripts. Our findings highlight an opportunity to better understand how conference time and investigator effort translate into downstream scholarly output.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level IV.

item.title: Community Paramedics Addressing the Evolving Opioid Crisis: A Case Series Addressing the Kratom Derivatives 7-Hydroxymitragynine and MGM-15.
item.description:
Prehosp Emerg Care | Tier 2 Filtered [Prehospital] [weak match]
Gormley MA, Wampler WR, Darby T et al.

Concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15) are derived from the primary psychoactive alkaloid in kratom, and until recently were sold over the counter with kratom products. These highly potent kratom derivatives can produce opioid-like dependence, but evidence around prehospital treatment of 7-OH and MGM-15 withdrawal symptoms remains limited. This case series assesses two cases of community paramedics (CPs) providing treatment and linkage to care for individuals in acute opioid withdrawal from 7-OH and MGM-15. In our first case a 74-year-old individual called 9-1-1 experiencing acute opioid-like withdrawal symptoms after abruptly discontinuing over the counter 7-OH following six months of progressively escalating use. Connection was made with a prehospital buprenorphine program (PBAP) and the CP administered 24mg of buprenorphine and expedited connection to outpatient treatment with medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD). Our second case involved a 38-year-old individual who called a CP requesting expedited linkage to MOUD following a period of escalating use of 7-OH and MGM-15. This patient was linked to MOUD treatment within 48 hours of contacting the CP and required 32mg/8mg of buprenorphine/naloxone to treat severe opioid withdrawal symptoms after discontinued use of MGM-15 tablets. Both patients were retained in MOUD treatment at 30 days. These cases describe use of CP-based PBAPs addressing severe 7-OH withdrawal and expediting treatment to outpatient MOUD, highlighting that concentrated over the counter 7-OH products can produce physical opioid dependence leading to opioid use disorder, and requiring full-dose buprenorphine induction which may be considered within existing prehospital opioid withdrawal treatment protocols. Additional research is necessary to characterize withdrawal from concentrated 7-OH products and to determine implications for PBAP protocols and 7-OH dosing in the United States.

item.title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.
item.description:
Prehosp Emerg Care | Tier 2 Filtered [Cardiac Arrest, Prehospital] [weak match]
Kimbrell JM, Kreinbrook JA, Robinson AE et al.

Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

item.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [Cardiac Arrest, General Trauma, Penetrating, Systems/QI] [strong match]
Khoschnau S, AlMadani A, Mekkodathil A et al.

BACKGROUND: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).

CONCLUSIONS: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

item.title: Clinical outcomes of combined MPFL-reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using hamstring autograft versus isolated MPFL in adolescents with patella alta: a retrospective comparative study.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [weak match]
Salem H, Ali EMS, Metwally O et al.

BACKGROUND: Patella alta is a major risk factor for recurrent patellar dislocation in adolescents. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of isolated medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction with those of MPFL reconstruction augmented by medial patellotibial ligament (MPTL)-distalization, both using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft, in adolescent patients with patella alta.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 28 adolescent patients (mean age 11.2 ± 1.6 years; 9 males, 19 females) treated for recurrent patellar dislocation between May 2020 and July 2025. All patients had patella alta (Caton-Deschamps index > 1.2) and a history of at least one dislocation, with varying degrees of trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types A-B). All patients underwent MPFL reconstruction using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft harvested with preservation of its native distal tibial insertion, fixed via a single oblique transpatellar tunnel and femoral interference-screw fixation proximal to the distal femoral physis. Group A (n=14) underwent isolated MPFL reconstruction. Group B (n=14) underwent the same MPFL reconstruction with an additional MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization step using the same graft, secured by trans-osseous periosteal suture at the lateral patella. Surgical techniques emphasized physeal spare during reconstruction. Preoperative and postoperative assessments included the Kujala score, Lysholm score, Caton-Deschamps index, and sulcus angle. Follow-up averaged 12- 24 months. CT was performed using a low-dose pediatric protocol specifically for TT-TG measurement and trochlear bony morphology; MRI was used for soft-tissue and cartilage assessment. Group assignment was not randomized; patients with more pronounced patella alta and higher-grade clinical instability were preferentially treated with the combined procedure.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in functional scores. In Group (A), Kujala scores improved from 59.3 ± 8.3 to 84.3 ± 5.1, and Lysholm scores from 50.3 ± 7.5 to 74.7 ± 9.3. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.27 to 1.20. In Group (B), Kujala scores improved from 56.2 ± 7.4 to 88.9 ± 4.5, and Lysholm scores from 51.4 ± 7.6 to 87.4 ± 6.2. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.28 to 1.11, indicating better patellar height correction. Complications occurred in 36% of Group A and 21% of Group B. Recurrent instability occurred in 2 patients (14%) in Group A and 1 patient (7%) in Group B; all were subluxation episodes managed non-operatively, and no revision surgery was required.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that MPFL reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using a hamstring autograft yields greater functional improvements, superior patella alta correction, and fewer complications compared to isolated MPFL reconstruction in adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective comparative study; level IV.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study is a retrospective comparative cohort study and does not meet the definition of a clinical trial as per the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) guidelines, as it involves retrospective analysis of routinely collected clinical data without prospective intervention or randomization.

item.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma, Systems/QI] [strong match]
Hierl K, Thiedemann C, Kerschbaum M et al.

PURPOSE: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs.

METHODS: Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate.

RESULTS: DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A).

CONCLUSION: Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

item.title: Guideline adherence in helicopter versus ground emergency medical services: an indication-based analysis of 129,783 patients from the TraumaRegister DGU
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma, Haemorrhage, Prehospital, Systems/QI, Thoracic] [weak match]
Faul P, Hagebusch P, Lefering R et al.

BACKGROUND: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) are associated with higher intervention rates and improved access to specialized trauma centers compared with ground emergency medical services (GEMS). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect increased intervention intensity alone or more consistent implementation of guideline-recommended care. This study aimed to compare rates of selected guideline-recommended prehospital trauma interventions between HEMS and GEMS using a nationwide trauma registry.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study was based on data from the TraumaRegister DGU

RESULTS: Patients transported by HEMS were younger and more severely injured than those transported by GEMS (mean ISS 23.5 vs. 20.8; ISS ≥ 16: 72.9% vs. 65.4%) and more frequently presented with impaired consciousness and shock. Across all predefined indication-based subgroups, HEMS was associated with higher rates of the evaluated interventions, including advanced airway management in patients with impaired consciousness (96.5% vs. 82.9%), overall chest tube placement in patients with thoracic injuries consistent with pneumothorax (50.5% vs. 40.9%), with substantially higher rates of prehospital chest tube placement in HEMS (14.0% vs. 5.5%), pelvic stabilization in patients with pelvic injuries of AIS severity 3-5 (56.7% vs. 44.0%), cervical spine immobilization in cervical spine injuries (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and tranexamic acid administration in suspected major bleeding (48.7% vs. 22.8%).

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide trauma registry analysis, HEMS was consistently associated with higher rates of selected guideline-related interventions across predefined indication-based subgroups. By focusing on patients with predefined guideline-related indications, the present study aimed to improve comparability between HEMS and GEMS beyond crude intervention frequencies. Nevertheless, the observed differences should be interpreted in the context of the observational study design and residual indication-related confounding. Higher intervention rates do not necessarily indicate superior guideline adherence or quality of care in individual patients.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

item.title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma, Systems/QI] [weak match]
Herold J, Lorenz ED, Eymann H et al.

BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.

RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

item.title: Cluster Versus Individual Randomization in Prehospital, Emergency and Critical Care Trials: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
item.description:
Crit Care Med | Tier 2 Filtered [Prehospital] [strong match]
Lønstrup S, Petersen PL, Bruun NH et al.

OBJECTIVES: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings.

DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase.

DATA SELECTION: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Using absolute ln(odds ratio [OR]) for mortality and absolute Hedges' g for the secondary outcome, mean differences (MDs) in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs were analyzed using mixed regression models, presented with 95% CIs. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT). We included 65 meta-analyses in quantitative analyses, encompassing 212 randomized clinical trials (39 cRCTs and 173 iRCTs) and 315,276 patients. No statistically significant difference in absolute ln(OR) for mortality between cRCTs and iRCTs was found (MD, -0.110; 95% CI, -0.093 to 0.313). For length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, a significant difference in absolute Hedges' g was found (MD, -0.202; 95% CI, -0.392 to -0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to compare the frequency and types of adverse safety events (ASEs) and potential harm in a diverse population of pediatric emergency medical services (EMS) encounters. As a secondary aim we evaluated the association between prehospital pediatric emergency care coordinators (PECCs) in EMS agencies on the frequency, type and harm severity of ASEs.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of EMS and hospital records for children <18 years who received care from 15 EMS agencies from 2019 to 2023, using a validated ASE chart review tool. Frequency and types of ASEs associated with three different categories of clinical interventions (procedures, medication, and fluid administration) were captured. ASEs were assigned to three severities of harm: Harm Unlikely, Mild Temporary Harm, or Permanent/Severe Harm. EMS Physicians verified ASEs and harm severity.

RESULTS: There were 2219 records included in the analysis, 995 from PECC agencies (44.8%). Median patient age was 12.5 years (IQR 6-15). In total, 551 (55.4%; CI: 52.3, 58.5) PECC agency patients had a procedure compared to 328 patients of agencies without a PECC (26.8%; CI: 24.3, 29.3; p < 0.001). Compared to non-PECC agency patients, PECC agency patients were more likely to receive medications (23.4% vs 7.7%, p< 0.001) and receive intravenous fluids (12.9% vs 4.6%, p< 0.001). In total, 290 ASEs were identified, the most frequent of which was the failure to perform a procedure or administer a medication or fluids (43.1%, CI: 37.4, 48.8). There were differences between PECC and non-PECC agencies in the frequency of ASEs in procedures (13.7% vs, 20.0%, p = 0.003). The assigned severity of ASE Mild Temporary and Permanent/Severe Harm was lower for procedures in PECC versus non-PECC agencies, respectively (28.6%, CI: 29.5, 48.5 and 63.3%, 95% CI: 69.6, 88.4, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared to non-PECC agency care, pediatric care by PECC agencies was associated with more procedures, medication and fluid administration, but fewer ASEs for procedures and lower severity of harm when an ASE occurred. These results indicate that the PECC role may be associated with increased interventions and a reduction in harm associated with procedural care.

item.description:
Acad Emerg Med | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma, Haemorrhage, Prehospital, Systems/QI] [strong match]
Honnef G, Zoidl P, Hallmann B et al.

BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Early trauma-induced coagulopathy (eTIC) is a major contributor to hemorrhage-related mortality after severe trauma. Viscoelastic testing using thromboelastography (TEG) has been increasingly implemented in trauma resuscitation; however, its prognostic value compared with conventional coagulation testing remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the ability of TEG parameters to detect eTIC, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperfibrinolysis in severely injured trauma patients. In addition, we assessed their prognostic performance for transfusion requirements and mortality compared with conventional laboratory parameters.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS: Severely injured adult trauma patients admitted to the resuscitation room of a Level I trauma center, between January 2019 and October 2024 were screened.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS: Primary outcomes were detection of eTIC (INR > 1.2), severe coagulopathy (INR > 1.5), hypofibrinogenemia (< 200 mg/dL), and thrombocytopenia (< 100,000/μL). Secondary outcomes included the ability of coagulation parameters to predict the need for transfusion of ≥ 5 units of packed red blood cells within the first 24 h after admission and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 262 patients were included; median ISS was 29 (IQR 23-41), and in-hospital mortality was 22.8%. eTIC was present in 31.5% of patients. TEG parameters showed moderate discriminatory performance for coagulopathy detection. For eTIC, maximum amplitude achieved an AUC of 0.73, while R-time achieved an AUC of 0.65. Predictive performance improved for severe coagulopathy, with R-time reaching an AUC of 0.81. Hyperfibrinolysis (LY30 > 7%) was uncommon (6.9%). Conventional laboratory parameters, particularly INR, consistently outperformed TEG-derived parameters for prediction of transfusion requirements (AUC 0.85) and mortality (AUC 0.79).

CONCLUSION: In severely injured trauma patients, conventional coagulation testing, particularly INR, demonstrated superior prognostic performance compared with individual TEG parameters. Viscoelastic testing may provide complementary information but did not replace standard laboratory testing for prediction of transfusion needs or mortality in this cohort.

item.title: Negative pressure wound therapy for the prevention of surgical site complications in emergency laparotomies: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
World J Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [Procedures] [weak match]
Rey Chaves CE, Orozco Chamorro CM, Ramírez-Giraldo C et al.

INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are common after emergency laparotomy and are associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged recovery, and increased health care costs. Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been increasingly used prophylactically on closed incisions in high-risk surgical patients; however, evidence supporting its effectiveness after emergency laparotomy remains heterogeneous. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to reassess the effectiveness of NPWT compared with standard postoperative dressings for the prevention of SSI and other wound-related complications following emergency laparotomy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published from April 2, 2022, to December 10, 2025, updating a prior review. Randomized clinical trials and comparative observational studies evaluating NPWT versus standard dressings in adult patients undergoing emergency laparotomy were included. The primary outcome was SSI. Secondary outcomes included superficial and deep SSI, wound dehiscence, seroma, hematoma, and length of hospital stay. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies involving 5371 patients were included, of whom 2528 received NPWT. NPWT was associated with a significantly lower risk of SSI compared with standard dressings (risk ratio, 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.68), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I² = 68%). NPWT was also associated with reductions in superficial and deep SSI, seroma formation, and wound dehiscence, but not with organ/space SSI, hematoma, or length of hospital stay. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent direction of effect. Funnel plot asymmetry and a significant Egger test suggested small-study effects.

CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing emergency laparotomy, prophylactic NPWT applied to closed incisions was associated with a lower risk of SSI and several wound-related complications compared with standard postoperative dressings. item.title: Fatigue, Anxiety and Depression 12 Months After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population Based Cohort Study.
item.description:

AIM: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms.

METHODS: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work.

RESULTS: Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

BACKGROUND: The smart advanced life support (SALS) program was introduced to provide prehospital advanced life support under real-time video-assisted physician direction for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used difference-in-differences and event-study analyses with data from the OHCA surveillance system in South Korea and included adult OHCA cases (aged ≥19 years) from 2 years before through 4 years after SALS implementation in August 2015. Event-study analyses suggested differential pre-intervention trends for prehospital time, but not for the other outcomes.

CONCLUSION: SALS regions showed greater increases in prehospital time and prehospital ROSC without significant improvements in survival to discharge or favorable neurological outcome, but the finding for prehospital time should be interpreted cautiously because differential pre-intervention trends were observed.

OBJECTIVE: Although recognised as a leading cause of death and disability, it is unclear whether current treatment strategies have improved outcomes from blunt moderate to severe traumatic brain injuries (msTBI) due to a lack of available epidemiological data. This study sought to determine if in-hospital mortality and early functional outcomes of msTBI patients have changed over 20 years. METHODS: A longitudinal cohort study using The Alfred Health Trauma Registry data. Subjects were aged 16-70 years with blunt msTBI (Head Abbreviated Injury Scale 3-5) admitted to The Alfred Trauma Service between 1 January 2002 and 31 December 2021.

RESULTS: A total of 8222 patients presented with msTBI over the period, with 692 deaths (8.5%). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality decreased from 12.1% in 2002 to 4.0% in 2021 (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.97, p < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the odds of death even after adjusting for injury severity (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.99, p < 0.0001). The proportion of patients discharged to home increased from 30.6% to 60.8% over the period (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: There was a reduction in in-hospital mortality and an increase in the proportion discharged home for adults hospitalised with msTBI at The Alfred Hospital over the last two decades. These results foster optimism for the care of neurotrauma patients, but further research is required to identify the modifiable factors associated with these improved outcomes.

item.description:

BACKGROUND: Evidence on the management of bezoar ileus in patients who have already undergone abdominal surgery is limited. We reviewed conservative and surgical pathways in clinically selected patients, with particular attention to patient selection criteria and how each pathway was defined.

METHODS: We reviewed 80 patients with CT-confirmed bezoar ileus and previous abdominal surgery who were treated between January 2010 and December 2021. Twenty-six completed conservative treatment, and 54 underwent surgery. In practice, conservative treatment was used for clinically stable patients without peritonitis or CT signs suggesting ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, provided that close clinical monitoring was possible. Conservative treatment included bowel rest, intravenous fluids, electrolyte correction, symptom-directed medication and nasogastric decompression when needed. Failure was defined by clinical deterioration, persistent or worsening obstruction, inability to tolerate oral intake, or new radiological concern. The primary outcome was clinical resolution during the index admission. Secondary outcomes were hospitalisation, in-hospital mortality, postoperative complications and readmission after discharge.

RESULTS: The treatment groups were not equivalent at baseline. Patients treated surgically more often had gastric bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 0/26, p = 0.002), multiple bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 1/26, 3.8%, p = 0.009) and greater small-bowel dilatation (median 4.0 cm vs. 3.4 cm, p = 0.014). All 26 patients in the conservative pathway completed the index admission without operation, although routine radiological confirmation of resolution was not performed. Median hospitalisation was 4 days (IQR 4-5) in the surgical group and 7 days (6-8) in the conservative group (p < 0.001); this difference should be interpreted in the context of clinical selection and local practice. Postoperative complications occurred in 11/54 surgical patients (20.4%), including two deaths from pulmonary embolism. Among discharged patients, readmission did not differ significantly between groups (13/52, 25.0% after surgery vs. 5/26, 19.2% after conservative treatment; p = 0.776). Exploratory regression findings were treated as hypothesis-generating only.

CONCLUSIONS: Conservative treatment may be feasible in selected stable patients with bezoar ileus after previous abdominal surgery. Surgery remains appropriate for patients with peritonitis, suspected ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, clinical deterioration, or failure of conservative management. Because treatment was not protocolised and the groups differed at baseline, the findings should be read as observational and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence that either strategy is superior.

BACKGROUND: Reported incidence of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) after severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) approaches one-third, largely from cohorts that excluded early deaths. Predictors and resource consequences remain unclear. We identified predictors of PSH development and associations between diagnosis, PSH Assessment Measure (PSH-AM) subscores [clinical features scale (CFS) and diagnosis likelihood tool (DLT)], and resource utilization.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary care center intensive care unit (ICU) (October 2020-September 2025), stratified by PSH diagnosis. Two reviewers assigned PSH-AM scores. PSH cannot be diagnosed until the syndrome declares itself over days, so exposure is conditioned on survival; mortality is reported descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of PSH diagnosis. Log-transformed linear regressions estimated associations of PSH diagnosis and subscores with hospital length of stay (LOS), ICU LOS, and ventilator days. Thirty-day composite outcomes, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and landmark analysis evaluated robustness.

RESULTS: Of 509 patients with severe TBI, 86 (17%) developed PSH. Younger age [odds ratio (OR): 0.97 (95% CI: 0.96-0.98); P<0.001) and higher ISS [1.05 (1.02-1.07); P<0.001] independently predicted PSH. PSH was associated with longer hospital LOS (372.9%), ICU LOS (278.3%), and more ventilator days (266.4%; all P<0.001). Mortality was 11.6% (PSH) versus 35.9% (non-PSH). IPTW demonstrated PSH had fewer days alive and out of hospital (-46.8%; P<0.001) and landmark analysis highlighted fewer ventilator-free days (-40.2%; P=0.0097) and ICU-free days (-46.9%; P<0.001). Higher DLT subscores were associated with longer hospital (36.3%; P=0.001) and ICU (23.3%; P=0.005) stays, whereas the CFS subscore showed no associations.

CONCLUSIONS: The PSH diagnosis is contingent on survival. Younger patients with severe TBI who survive their initial injuries are more likely to develop PSH and occupy hospital beds meaningfully longer. The diagnosis likelihood tool, not the clinical features scale, tracks with that burden.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.
